name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
description: A central government scheme that provides income support to landholding farmer families to help cover farming inputs and household needs. The government bears the full cost of the transfers.
eligibility: Landholding farmer families with cultivable land in their own names (family = husband, wife and minor children). Institutional landholders and certain categories such as constitutional post holders, serving or retired government employees (excluding multi-tasking/Group D staff), income taxpayers and practising professionals are excluded (per Revised FAQ, Nov 2021).
benefits: Income support transferred directly into the beneficiary's bank account in instalments.
howToApply: Submit details to the village Patwari/revenue officials or designated agency, or self-register through Farmers' Corner on pmkisan.gov.in; eKYC is mandatory for registered farmers (OTP-based eKYC on the portal or biometric eKYC at a CSC).

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
description: A flagship government-sponsored crop insurance scheme launched on 18 February 2016 that protects farmers from crop losses caused by natural risks such as drought, flood, cyclone, hailstorm, pests and diseases. It covers the crop cycle from pre-sowing to post-harvest.
eligibility: Loanee farmers sanctioned seasonal agricultural operation loans (enrolment mandatory) and non-loanee farmers, including those with non-standard KCC-linked crop loans or no crop loan, and loanee farmers who opt in voluntarily.
benefits: Insurance cover for yield losses on standing crops, prevented sowing, post-harvest losses (cut-and-spread condition) and localized calamities; the government subsidises the remainder of the premium beyond the farmer's share.
howToApply: Enrol online through the National Crop Insurance Portal (pmfby.gov.in) or via banks, insurance companies and Common Service Centres; queries via the helpline 14447.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
description: A scheme begun in 1998 under which farmers get credit from the banking system through a single window for cultivation and other needs. The revised KCC scheme was launched on 18 December 2020.
eligibility: Owner-cultivator farmers (individual or joint borrowers); tenant farmers, oral lessees and share croppers; and SHGs or JLGs of farmers, including tenant farmers and share croppers.
benefits: Short-term credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses and produce marketing; credit for household consumption and farm asset maintenance; investment credit for agriculture and allied activities; ATM-enabled RuPay card with one-time documentation.
howToApply: Fill in a one-page form (basic data pre-filled from PM-KISAN records) and add a copy of the land record and crop details; forms are available from bank websites, the agriculture department website or the PM-KISAN portal, and CSCs can submit the form to the bank branch.
sourceName: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (PIB factsheet)

name: Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)
description: A Central Sector Scheme that helps farmers obtain short-term credit at affordable interest rates through Kisan Credit Cards. The Union Cabinet approved continuing the Interest Subvention component for FY 2025-26.
eligibility: Farmers availing short-term loans through Kisan Credit Cards; benefits extend to animal husbandry and fisheries loans as described by the Government.
benefits: Interest subvention to eligible lending institutions so that farmers receive short-term KCC loans at a subsidised rate, with a Prompt Repayment Incentive for timely repayment.
howToApply: No separate application stated; availed through the Kisan Credit Card loan from a participating bank or cooperative.
sourceName: Prime Minister's Office (Union Cabinet decision) / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
description: Launched on 19 February 2015, the scheme helps State Governments issue soil health cards to farmers, giving the nutrient status of their soil and recommended nutrient doses to improve soil health and fertility.
eligibility: The stated aim is to cover all farmers and every farm holding; no separate eligibility conditions are listed. Village youth and farmers up to 40 years of age can set up soil health laboratories under the related component.
benefits: A printed soil health report per holding with crop and fertiliser recommendations; support from experts for corrective measures.
howToApply: Cards are issued by State Governments after soil sampling and testing at soil testing laboratories; the scheme portal is soilhealth.dac.gov.in. No formal application process is described.
sourceName: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (PIB factsheet)

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM)
description: Approved on 19 February 2019 to provide energy and water security to farmers, raise their incomes and reduce diesel use in agriculture. It has three components: small solar power plants, standalone solar agricultural pumps and solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps.
eligibility: Component A: individual farmers, cooperatives, panchayats and FPOs. Component B: individual farmers and groups such as Water User Associations in off-grid areas without an electricity source for irrigation. Component C: feeder-level solarisation run by DISCOMs or RESCOs.
benefits: Central financial assistance for solar pumps and feeder solarisation, and income from leasing or setting up solar plants on farmland; remote monitoring of pumps.
howToApply: For Component A, DISCOMs invite applications from interested beneficiaries. For other components contact your state implementing agency or DISCOM.
sourceName: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
description: A medium to long term debt financing facility for investment in viable projects relating to post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
eligibility: Intended beneficiaries include Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies, Farmer Producer Organisations, agriculture entrepreneurs and start-ups, among others; APMCs were later included.
benefits: Interest subvention and CGTMSE credit guarantee support on eligible loans, a project management unit for handholding, and convergence with other central and state schemes.
howToApply: Online single window facility in collaboration with participating lending institutions (commercial banks, cooperative banks, RRBs, small finance banks, NCDC and NBFCs) via the AIF portal.

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
description: A scheme under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture, launched in 2015, that promotes organic farming through a cluster approach with training, certification and market linkages.
eligibility: Farmers and institutions forming organic clusters; the scheme targets small and marginal farmers (landholding up to two hectares as stated on the source page).
benefits: Financial assistance over three years for organic inputs, marketing and packaging, certification and residue analysis, and training, with input support paid through direct benefit transfer.
howToApply: Approach your Regional Council, which helps with enrolment and certification; Councils compile applications into an Annual Action Plan submitted to the Ministry. No direct online application for individual farmers is described.

name: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)
description: Launched on 1 July 2015 to expand assured irrigation, improve on-farm water use efficiency and promote water conservation. Components include AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Watershed Development and Per Drop More Crop.
eligibility: No general eligibility criteria listed; the Per Drop More Crop micro-irrigation component targets small and marginal farmers in particular.
benefits: Irrigation infrastructure, watershed development and financial assistance for drip and sprinkler micro-irrigation systems, with higher assistance for small and marginal farmers.
howToApply: No application process is described on the source page; guidelines are at pmksy.gov.in and state agriculture/horticulture departments handle micro-irrigation applications.
sourceName: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / Ministry of Jal Shakti

name: National Agriculture Market (eNAM)
description: A pan-India electronic trading portal, launched on 14 April 2016, that networks the existing APMC mandis to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.
eligibility: Farmers, traders, FPOs and APMC/mandi boards can register on the portal; no formal eligibility criteria are stated on the fetched pages.
benefits: Online competitive and transparent price discovery, e-payment directly into farmers' accounts, and a single window for APMC information such as arrivals, quality and prices.
howToApply: Register through the Registration link on enam.gov.in (Registration Guidelines and Operational Guidelines are published on the site); helpline 1800 270 0224.
sourceName: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (eNAM) / PIB

name: Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY)
description: A 'cafeteria scheme' approved by the Union Cabinet on 3 October 2024 (with Krishonnati Yojana) to promote sustainable agriculture, implemented through State Governments. It includes components such as Soil Health Management, Rainfed Area Development and Agro Forestry.
eligibility: Implemented through State Governments; no individual eligibility criteria are listed on the source page.
benefits: Funding to states for agriculture sector components, with flexibility to reallocate funds between components and approve Annual Action Plans in one go.
howToApply: No individual application stated; benefits are delivered through state agriculture departments.
sourceName: Prime Minister's Office (Union Cabinet decision) / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

name: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA)
description: Launched in September 2018, a price-support framework to ensure remunerative prices for farmers. It brings together the Price Support Scheme, Price Stabilization Fund, Price Deficiency Payment Scheme and Market Intervention Scheme.
eligibility: Under the Price Support Scheme, eligibility is limited to registered farmers with valid land records.
benefits: Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra at MSP when market prices fall below it, price-deficiency payments directly to bank accounts, and market intervention for perishables.
howToApply: Registration is required for Price Support Scheme procurement; steps are not given on the source page. Check with your state procurement agency or the Ministry.

name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
description: A Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits, vegetables, spices, flowers, mushrooms, coconut, cashew, cocoa, bamboo and other crops.
eligibility: Individual farmers, farmer groups, FIGs, FPOs, SHGs and cooperatives; for specified components also firms, companies, local bodies, APMCs, marketing boards and State Governments.
benefits: Subsidy tied to approved cost norms for horticulture production, post-harvest and marketing infrastructure, with higher rates in North Eastern and Himalayan States, tribal and hilly areas.
howToApply: States set up a transparent system for receiving applications; contact your State Horticulture Mission or district horticulture office for forms and contacts.
sourceName: National Horticulture Board / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

name: Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)
description: A Central Sector Scheme to form and promote 10,000 new FPOs by 2027-28 using a produce cluster approach, with SFAC supporting state governments and nine Implementing Agencies.
eligibility: Targets small, marginal and landless farmers; FPOs must be registered under Part IXA of the Companies Act or a state Co-operative Societies Act.
benefits: Financial assistance to FPOs over three years, matching equity grant, credit guarantee for project loans, five years of handholding by Cluster Based Business Organisations and capacity building.
howToApply: Not for individual farmers directly; Implementing Agencies and Cluster Based Business Organisations aggregate and register FPOs. See sfacindia.com for guidelines.

name: National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)
description: A standalone Centrally Sponsored Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet to promote chemical-free farming using local livestock-integrated methods and diversified crops adapted to local agro-ecology.
eligibility: No individual eligibility criteria stated; the mission targets farmers through Gram Panchayat clusters.
benefits: Training, Bio-input Resource Centres, model demonstration farms, Krishi Sakhi support and a simple certification system for natural farming produce.
howToApply: No application process stated; implemented through state agriculture departments and Gram Panchayat clusters.
sourceName: Prime Minister's Office (Union Cabinet decision) / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

name: Bihar Agriculture Department DBT Schemes (Krishi Input Grant, Diesel Subsidy, etc.)
description: The Agriculture Department of Bihar runs a Direct Benefit Transfer portal where farmers register and apply online for schemes such as Krishi Input Grant, Diesel Subsidy, agricultural mechanisation, micro-irrigation and horticulture schemes. Benefits are paid into the Aadhaar-linked bank account.
eligibility: Bihar farmers (raiyat or non-raiyat) aged 18 or older with a mobile number linked to Aadhaar and an active bank account; scheme-specific conditions vary.
benefits: Direct benefit transfer to the farmer's bank account under the listed schemes.
howToApply: Register online with OTP or biometrically at a Vasudha Kendra to obtain a 13-digit registration number, then log in with it and an OTP to apply when a scheme window is open.
sourceName: Department of Agriculture, Government of Bihar

name: Rajasthan Department of Agriculture Grant Schemes (Raj Kisan Sathi)
description: The Rajasthan Department of Agriculture lists grant schemes for agriculture, horticulture, agricultural marketing and animal husbandry on its Rajkisan portal, covering items such as farm ponds, irrigation pipelines, drip and sprinkler systems and solar pumps.
howToApply: Applications for agriculture, horticulture and marketing grant schemes are submitted online through the Raj Kisan Sathi portal, per a notice on the Rajkisan portal.
sourceName: Department of Agriculture, Government of Rajasthan

name: Maharashtra MahaDBT Farmer Schemes
description: The Government of Maharashtra's MahaDBT (Aaple Sarkar DBT) portal lists farmer schemes including micro-irrigation under PMKSY, the Sub-Mission on Farm Mechanization, NFSM, Rainfed Area Development and state schemes for SC and ST farmers.
howToApply: Register on the MahaDBT portal (Aadhaar OTP, biometric or non-Aadhaar), complete your profile, open 'All Schemes' and apply; track status under 'My Applied Scheme'. Scheme-specific eligibility is in each scheme's Government Resolution on the portal.
